# Benchmarks

*Generated by `scripts/gen_bench_pages.py` from the `oml-bench/1` results in `eval/bench/results/`; do not edit by hand. Regenerate with `python scripts/gen_bench_pages.py`, and CI fails when this page differs from what it writes.*

The default search pipeline is `bm25-postings` (the deployment's `search.default` when unset; [settings](../operations/configuration.md)). It scores within 0.003 nDCG@10 of `bm25` on the quality suites and is the one pipeline an index serves under row security, so its latency grows slowest with the rows; the pipelines that score higher read every readable row's stored lexemes or add a model stage. Choice of default: ADR-0049 d9 and [the benchmark report](https://github.com/e8kor/open-memory-lab/blob/main/eval/bench/REPORT.md).

## Methodology

Every number went through the served path: memories written over HTTP by an agent key, promoted by reviewer keys of other principals, and recalled through `oml_read` over `/mcp`, one query at a time. Latency is the client's wall time per call, in milliseconds. Reference rows are offline and have no latency. Every suite page lists all pipelines, the run's commit and host, and its limits.

??? note "The latency ceiling"

    **The latency ceiling.** Under row security no text index serves a recall: `@@`, `%` and `ts_rank` are not leakproof (ADR-0034 d13), so every pipeline but `bm25-postings` reads the stored lexemes of every row the key may read, and its cost grows with those rows. Storing the lexemes made a row several times cheaper, not free: the scale lane measured an every-word match over a stored `simple` vector past 50 ms near 70,000 readable rows (`bench/scale/REPORT-baseline.md`), and `bm25` reads more per row than that match, so on abstract-length text it crosses the line far sooner, as the tables show. Latency at scale is not solved by stored lexemes. `bm25-postings` (ADR-0052) reads integer postings, which row security lets an index serve, so its cost follows the postings it reads: 25.5 ms p95 at 99,721 readable rows against `bm25`'s 485 ms (`bench/scale/REPORT.md`).
